title: bug: the scheduler package-boundary scan throws on a regex literal inside a template expression, and the throw blinds the rest of the walk
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-08 21:12Z by worker-bcaa6d5e, foreground, no lease (single test file):

  pnpm exec vitest run packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts
  Tests  1 failed | 55 passed (56)   EXIT 1
  > keeps scheduler registrars behind the package-root import boundary
  Error: boundary scan failed for apps\daemon\src\deployment\deploy-candidate-environment.ts: Error: unterminated quoted source token

THE NAMED DAEMON FILE IS NOT THE DEFECT. `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-environment.ts:74` is valid TypeScript:
  .map(([name, value]) => `${name}='${value.replace(/'/gu, "'\\''")}'\n`)

THE DEFECT IS IN THE SCANNER. `packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts:99` `templateExpressionEnd()` — the brace matcher that finds the end of a `${...}` — has branches for `'`, `"`, nested backticks, `//` and `/* */`, and NO REGULAR-EXPRESSION BRANCH. `sourceTokens()` at :168 already has one (`canStartRegularExpression` + `readRegularExpression`); the omission exists only in the template-expression scanner.

MECHANISM: walking `value.replace(/'/gu, ...)`, at the `/` of `/'/gu` the `next` char is `'`, so it is neither `//` nor `/*`; control falls to `else`, steps ONE char forward, and lands ON the quote inside the regex. The `'` branch then fires `readQuoted` from there, pairing that quote against the next `'` in the file (inside `"'\\''"`). Pairing stays off-by-one until a quote opens a run that hits end-of-line, where `readQuoted` (:92) throws `unterminated quoted source token`.

MINIMAL REPRO, no daemon involved:  const x = `${s.replace(/'/gu, "y")}`;
Any regex literal containing a quote character, inside a template expression.

THE SILENT HALF IS WORSE THAN THE RED: the scan `throw`s on the FIRST unreadable file, so one such file blinds the boundary check for EVERY file after it in walk order. This test is the fence keeping `@moe/scheduler` internals out of the rest of the tree; while it is red it is also not checking a scan-order tail of the repo at all.

SCOPE: test-only, one function, one file. Restores coverage rather than adding it. Filed by an idle worker seat with no claimed row; the chat escalation (msg-67929259, chan-ced99359) returned `routingTargets: []` because the channel Loop Guard had already capped, so it notified nobody — this row is the escalation. Reported unowned by qa-2702df88 as the board's only reproducible red.
definitionOfDone: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts` is EXIT 0 with all cases passing, quoted with its real output, and `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-environment.ts` is UNCHANGED by this row — the daemon file is correct TypeScript and editing it would hide the scanner defect rather than fix it.

`templateExpressionEnd()` consumes a regular-expression literal as ONE token, gated the same way `sourceTokens()` gates its own regex branch. State in a step note whether the gating helper was reused or duplicated, and if duplicated, why.

A regression case asserts the minimal shape directly — a regex literal containing a quote character inside a `${...}` — alongside the existing table at :264. Assert on the SCANNER's result for that source text, not on the daemon file, so the arm survives that file changing or moving.

AN ARM PROVES THE SCAN DOES NOT SILENTLY STOP EARLY. The current failure mode hides every file after the first unreadable one; a fix that only removes the throw would leave that hole open. Assert the scan reaches a known-last file, or that the count of files scanned equals the count enumerated.

Confirm by measurement whether the blinded tail contained any real boundary violation that was being hidden: run the fixed scan and report the number of files now scanned versus before, and name any violation it newly reports. If none, say so explicitly — a clean result here is a finding, not an absence.
No net new production code. The whole change is inside `packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts`.

implementationPlan.description: Fix templateExpressionEnd only for lexical recognition: reuse canStartRegularExpression and readRegularExpression after the existing comment branches so a regex literal is consumed atomically and its quotes/braces cannot affect template depth. Track the expression's preceding significant SourceToken context while advancing: skip whitespace/comments, consume full identifiers with identifierStart/identifierPart, retain string and punctuation classifications, and handle a nested literal template as a string or an interpolated template's terminal } as punctuation, matching sourceTokens' regex-gating context. Maintain brace depth only outside quoted/comment/template/regex tokens. Preserve existing lexical failures; no catch-and-ignore, unconditional slash-as-regex, eager prefix re-tokenization, parser dependency, or change to daemon input. Reuse the helper and existing prefix sets rather than duplicating the gating policy; explain that choice in the step note and one concise inline why-comment. Avoid changing sourceTokens or broader unsupported-language semantics unless the named controls prove it necessary; report any additional scope need before taking another path. DoD 2/3/6.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 GREEN. `pnpm exec vitest run packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts` -> EXIT 0; "Test Files  1 passed (1)"; "Tests  100 passed (100)"; Duration 1.25s. `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck` -> EXIT 0 (tsc --project tsconfig.json, no output). Was 28 failed | 72 passed at step 2.

GATING HELPER: REUSED, NOT DUPLICATED — answering DoD item 2 explicitly. `templateExpressionEnd` now calls the SAME `canStartRegularExpression(tokens)` gate and the SAME `readRegularExpression` reader that `sourceTokens` already used, and the same `identifierStart`/`identifierPart`/`regexPrefixIdentifiers`/`regexPrefixPunctuation` constants. No second copy of the policy exists, so the two scanners cannot drift. The regex branch sits AFTER both comment branches, exactly as in `sourceTokens`, so `//` and `/*` still win over a regex start.

WHY IT NEEDED MORE THAN ONE BRANCH: the gate is a function of the preceding significant token, and the old matcher kept no tokens at all. It now accumulates them the way `sourceTokens` does — whitespace and comments produce none (so they are not predecessors), identifiers are consumed whole, quoted strings become string tokens, everything else becomes single-character punctuation (so `2 / count` sees punctuation "2", not in the prefix set, and stays division). Brace depth is only touched outside quoted, comment, template and regex tokens, and the depth-zero `}` returns before being pushed.

ONE THIRD-PARTY SUBTLETY, handled by sharing rather than by restating: `sourceTokens` renders a nested template as a string token when it has a literal and as `{` + inner tokens + `}` when it is interpolated, and that difference decides the gate for a following `/`. I extracted those six lines verbatim into `pushTemplateTokens(tokens, template)` and now call it from BOTH scanners. That is the only edit to `sourceTokens` and it is a pure extraction: identical bytes, identical order, no semantic change. The alternative was duplicating the policy in the matcher, which the step forbids. Both `` `t` / count `` (string predecessor) and `` `${z}` / count `` (punctuation "}" predecessor) are covered as division cases and pass.

MIRRORED QUIRK, deliberately not "improved": like `sourceTokens`, the matcher pushes NO token after consuming a regex literal, so the predecessor seen by a following `/` is whatever preceded the regex. Diverging here would have been a semantic change to shared gating outside this row's scope. No unconditional slash-as-regex, no prefix re-tokenization, no parser dependency, no catch-and-ignore: `readRegularExpression`'s and `readQuoted`'s throws still propagate, which the fail-closed arm now pins at the matcher layer.

PERFORMANCE, measured because the repository arm has a 30s bound and previously died after 958 files: the full 4109-file walk plus all 100 cases runs in 1.25s total.

No production source touched. `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-environment.ts` untouched (DoD 1) and no net new production code (DoD 6). Foreign dirt untouched.
